STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of roasted or fried sweet potato (or similar orange root vegetable) cubes on a white square plate. No other dishes are part of this meal.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White square plate, roughly 24 cm across. Area ≈ 24 x 24 x 0.85 (square with rounded corners) ≈ 490 cm^2; using a round-equivalent of 24 cm diameter gives 452 cm^2. Use ~470 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Roasted sweet potato cubes (about 20 pieces, some with browned skin), a few light oil/seasoning specks.

STEP 4 - Area: Sweet potato cubes cover roughly 22% of the plate (the pile is compact, about 100 cm^2). Oil/seasoning residue is negligible (<1%). Total covered ≈ 22%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Pile of cubes, typical height ~2 cm over covered area. 100 cm^2 x 2 cm ≈ 200 ml gross.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut vegetable pieces, bulk density ~0.6 g/ml. 200 ml x 0.6 ≈ 120 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked sweet potato roasted/fried, ~110 kcal per 100 g (fried or oil-roasted ones run higher; plain roasted ~90). Use 110 kcal/100 g. 120 g x 1.1 ≈ 132 kcal. Add a small oil allowance of ~2 g x 884 ≈ 18 kcal. Total ≈ 150 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 20 cubes of sweet potato, roughly 1.5–2 cm each, is plausibly 100–130 g. A half-to-small portion is consistent with a plate that is only about a fifth covered. Plausible.

Total: about 120 g, about 150 kcal.
